facts.statement: Only a single fossil specimen, consisting of a slab and counterslab, is known for Shanweiniao.
facts.quote: There is one known fossil, a slab and counterslab.

facts.statement: The fossil was collected from the Dawangzhengzi Beds of the middle Yixian Formation in Lingyuan, Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Lower Cretaceous Dawangzhengzi Beds, middle Yixian Formation, from Lingyuan in the Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: The fossil is housed at the Dalian Natural History Museum with accession numbers DNHM D1878/1 and DNHM1878/2.
facts.quote: The fossil is in the collection of the Dalian Natural History Museum, and has accession number DNHM D1878/1 and DNHM1878/2.

facts.statement: The species name cooperorum honors Carl and Lynn Cooper for funding the study of Mesozoic birds in China.
facts.quote: The specific name, cooperorum, is after Carl and Lynn Cooper who donated funds to support the study of Mesozoic birds in China.

facts.statement: Only one fossil has been discovered, which consists of a slab and a counterslab.
facts.quote: Sólo un único fósil ha sido descubierto, una losa y una contralosa.

facts.statement: The time range for Shanweiniao is estimated from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago, spanning the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Although originally thought to be arboreal, Shanweiniao appears to have been terrestrial, similar to megapodes and larks.
facts.quote: Though originally interpreted as an arboreal bird, it appears to have been terrestrial in habits, ranking with taxa like megapodes and larks.

facts.statement: Researchers later stated that interpretations of Shanweiniao's tail morphology are speculative because the feathers of the holotype are incompletely preserved.
facts.quote: In a subsequent publication O'Connor et al. (2016) stated that interpretations of the tail morphology of this species are speculative due to incomplete preservation of the feathers of the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Shanweiniao is classified within the clade Longipterygidae, a group of long-beaked enantiornithean birds that also includes Longipteryx, Longirostravis, and Rapaxavis.
facts.quote: O'Connor et al. (2010) found that Shanweiniao is a close relative of Longipteryx, Longirostravis, and Rapaxavis, which together form a clade of long-beaked enantiornithean birds, the Longipterygidae.

facts.statement: Shanweiniao belongs to the family Longipterygidae.
Shanweiniao is classified in the subclass Enantiornithes.
Shanweiniao is classified in the class Aves.
